title: Polar Coordinates and Polar Graphs
seo_title: Precalculus Polar Coordinates and Graphs Worksheets (TEKS P.3D, P.3E)
standard_text: P.3D graph points in the polar coordinate system and convert between rectangular coordinates and polar coordinates; P.3E graph polar equations by plotting points and using technology
meta_desc: Free Precalculus polar coordinate worksheets for Texas TEKS P.3D and P.3E: convert polar and rectangular points and equations, equivalent polar points, and polar graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ.
key_sub: r = √(x² + y²); choose θ in the point's quadrant.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A polar point (r, θ) is r units from the pole at angle θ.
  • Polar to rectangular: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ.
  • Rectangular to polar: r = √(x2 + y2), tan θ = y ÷ x (choose θ in the quadrant of the point).
  • Graphs: r = a is a circle; r = a cos nθ is a rose with n petals if n is odd and 2n if n is even.

Examples

Example

(4, 2π3)

x = 4 cos(2π/3) = −2

y = 4 sin(2π/3) = 2√3

Answer: (−2, 2√3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping cos and sinx uses cos θ.
The wrong quadranttan−1 alone gives Quadrants I and IV.
Petals of a roseOdd n: n petals. Even n: 2n.

items.q: Which polar coordinates name the same point as (5, 2π3), using a negative r?
items.e: (−r, θ + π) is the same point as (r, θ): going backward from the opposite direction. (−5, 5π3).

items.q: Which point is not the same as (5, 5π6)?
items.e: (−r, θ) is the reflection through the pole, not the same point. (−5, 5π6).

items.q: Which polar coordinates name the same point as (5, 5π6)?

items.q: How many petals does the rose r = 3 sin 4θ have?
items.e: For r = a sin nθ: n petals if n is odd, 2n petals if n is even. Here n = 4, so 8.
It is a rose with 8 petals of length 4. r = 4 cos 4θ.
It is a limaçon with an inner loop, because |4| > |3|. The longest distance from the pole is 3 + 4 = 7. r = 3 + 4 sin θ.
It is a cardioid (heart shape). It points left, so the equation uses cos with a minus sign. r = 2 − 2 cos θ.

items.q: How many petals does the rose r = 4 sin 4θ have?
items.e: For r = a sin nθ: n petals if n is odd, 2n petals if n is even. Here n = 4, so 8.
It is a limaçon with an inner loop, because |6| > |4|. The longest distance from the pole is 4 + 6 = 10. r = 4 + 6 cos θ.
It is a cardioid (heart shape). It points right, so the equation uses cos with a plus sign. r = 2 + 2 cos θ.

It is a limaçon with an inner loop, because |5| > |3|. The longest distance from the pole is 3 + 5 = 8. r = 3 + 5 sin θ.
It is a cardioid (heart shape). It points up, so the equation uses sin with a plus sign. r = 3 + 3 sin θ.
